name: ui
description: Interfaces made of entities: rows and grids of cells, bars that fill, texts and bars that show a number of the game, and menus whose buttons raise actions. Nothing here is a particular HUD or menu: a game assembles its own.

components.name: Grid
components.description: Lays out the entities that have a Cell of the same group: cell number n goes in column n % columns and row n / columns, cell_width + spacing_x and cell_height + spacing_y apart, the first cell being centred on the Grid's own Position. columns 1 makes a column, a large number a row. A hotbar, an inventory, a list of buttons and a table are all grids with other numbers. group names an item of the game's "group" list (game.json lists).

components.name: Cell
components.description: An entity that a Grid of the same group places: index is its number in the grid, counted from 0.

components.name: Bind
components.description: Shows a number of the game: every tick, the value of field (written "module.Component.field", for example "pickup.Collector.score") of the entity tagged source is copied into this entity's Text value and into its Bar value, whichever it has. With own, the entity reads the field of itself instead of the entity tagged source: the number written on a tile, the health bar of a monster (put a Bind on the entity that has the Bar and the Health). A missing source or component leaves the value at 0.

components.name: Bar
components.description: A bar that fills as value goes from 0 to max: the entity's Sprite is made length * value / max long and thickness thick (the other way round when vertical). Give the Sprite a pivot_x of 0 (pivot_y of 1 when vertical) and the bar grows from its left (bottom) end, which sits on the Position. Put a Bind on the entity to show a number of the game.

components.name: Menu
components.description: The controller of one menu: the Buttons of the same group. They are read as a table, as they are laid out on the screen: the ones side by side (about the same height) make a row. left and right (actions of the game) move the focus along the row, up and down to the row above or below, to the button that is the nearest; buttons on top of each other count as one after the other, in the order of their numbers. accept presses the focused one; with use_pointer, the pointer (the actions pointer_x and pointer_y, in pixels) focuses the button it is over when it moves and click presses it. An action left out is none: nothing happens for it. group names an item of the game's "menu" list; wrap makes the focus go round. focused is the number of the focused button.

components.name: Button
components.description: A button of the menu of the same group: number order in the focus order, centred on the Position and width by height pixels big (for the pointer). Pressing it raises the action named by action (none when left out), which lasts one tick: a GoToScene that uses that action then changes the scene, an inventory or any rule can listen to it too. The entity's Sprite shows cell normal_frame, or focus_frame while the button is focused. A button that is not enabled cannot be focused, hovered or pressed, and shows disabled_frame (a Row turns its button off when the page has no item for it).

components.name: Pager
components.description: A list filled while the game runs (the games a launcher found, the players of a lobby), shown a page at a time. list names an item of the game's "runtime_list" list; page_size is how many Rows show it at once and page the one shown (0 is the first). The actions previous and next (an action left out is none) change the page, which never leaves 0 to pages - 1; pages is written for you, at least 1. menu names the game's "menu" whose Buttons are the Rows: the Row that has the focus becomes the selected item of the list, and stays selected when the focus goes to another button (Previous, Play...), so host.Call can act on it.

components.name: Row
components.description: One line of the Pager of the same list: it shows item number page * page_size + row of the list. The entity needs a text2d.Text and a text2d.Dynamic (written for you: the list and the item to show) and, to be chosen, a Button. When the page has no item for the row, the Button is switched off. item is written for you.

components.name: RowButton
components.description: A second button for a Row: it stands for the same item of the same Pager's list (an export icon beside each game, a delete button beside each save). Give it a Button; it is switched off when the page has no item for the row, and when it has the focus, or is pressed, the item of its row is the selected item of the list, so host.Call can act on it. It is a separate entity from the Row's own, so the two can be told apart and sit side by side (left and right move the focus from one to the other). item is written for you.

systems.name: layout
systems.description: Places the cells of every grid.

systems.name: bind
systems.description: Copies the bound numbers into the texts and bars that show them.

systems.name: fill
systems.description: Sizes the sprite of every bar from its value.

systems.name: menu
systems.description: Moves the focus of every menu and raises the action of the button that is pressed.

systems.name: pager
systems.description: Turns the pages of every Pager and gives each Row and RowButton its item, switching off the buttons that have none.

systems.name: select
systems.description: Makes the item of the focused Row (or RowButton) the selected item of its list.
